routes.reason: Source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1, R03.3 and R03.6, 18 items: the complete-local algebra the paper runs on — Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity with its additivity, support and equidimensionality bookkeeping, monomial ideals and the height computations of §3.6.3. All three stage ids exist and own exactly that. Keeping this apart from the arithmetic patching axioms is the right division, and it is what makes E44's multiplicity-convention defect (and the §6(12) correction to [LLHLM18] behind it) land on a single owner.

Source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7, by far the largest source route at 133 items: Kisin modules with descent data, shapes, the explicit charts of Tables 3–4, the components of the special fibre and the potentially crystalline rings. L7 already owns bounded-height lattice moduli and potentially semistable ring/component comparisons, so this is a refinement of an existing stage rather than a new one. Nine of the findings (E04–E09, E12, E46–E50) are about exactly these charts, and all nine belong here.

Source of CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.1, CC.2, CC.3 and CC.8 for the definite unitary tower, its Pontryagin and Schikhof duals, and the unitary adapter. Three items is the right size: §5.3 uses the tower as a black box, and the Hecke-algebra and level bookkeeping that E91–E94 and E99 report as under-specified is precisely what this route hands to the existing owner.

Part II of ReductiveAlgebraicGroups, 241 items, area representations (a galaxy id), brief 615 words. The title reproduces the parent's atlas title exactly. This is §4 of the paper — Q_1(μ), the translation principle, the socle and radical filtrations, the extension graph and the lattice-gauge machinery — and none of it is in the parent. It is also where the review's heaviest findings sit (E57, E60, E61, E64, E67–E69), which is the right place for them: they are statements about modular representation theory, not about Galois deformations.

Part II of AlgebraicModularFormsReductionAndSerreWeights, 165 items, brief 601 words. The title reproduces the parent's atlas title exactly. The area was corrected at the checkpoint from `modular`, which is an atlas group rather than a galaxy id, to `automorphic`, which is both a galaxy id and the value PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 uses for the same roadmap id; that correction stands. The remaining divergence between the two extractions is the topic half of the title (‘generic GL3 weights and Breuil lattices’ here against ‘generic Breuil–Mézard, Serre weights and GL3 lattices’ there), which the design job will have to settle; the parent prefix agrees.

Source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 for coherent Hartogs extension with full support, 6 items. The same owner already serves PAPER-GILLE-PARIMALA-26 and PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19, so this joins an existing proposal. The route is also what E89/E90's correction is about: the codimension-two extension needs full support, and stating it at this stage rather than inside §5.2 is the right placement.

Source of SF.2 for local cohomology: the comparison of the Ext-colimit definition with the localisation sequence, and flat base change for sections and ideal closures, 3 items. Distinct enough from route 6's Hartogs statement to deserve its own stage, and SF.2 exists.
